source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS Astronomical-Book fragments (4Q208-4Q211) where preserved; Ge'ez as fallback. NO continuous Greek witness for chs 72-82.
source.transliteration_convention: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic per Milik 1976 + Tigchelaar-García Martínez DJD XXXVI 2000; Ge'ez SBL convention.
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976, Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000, Drawnel 2011, Neugebauer 1985.

source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 77 — THE FOUR QUARTERS OF THE EARTH + their associations + seven great mountains + seven great rivers. **4Q210 frag 1 col. iii preserves substantial Aramaic parallel** — the four-quarters geography and the place-names of the seven mountains/rivers. CROSS-CORPUS to the seven-mountains geography of Mesopotamian + early Jewish cosmography.

verses.text_geez: ወቀዳማይተ፡ ይሰምይዋ፡ ምሥራቅ፡ እስመ፡ ቀዳማይት፡ ይእቲ፡ ወካልዕተ፡ ይሰምይዋ፡ ጾታ፡ እስመ፡ ህየ፡ ይትዐመጽ፡ እጅገ፡ ኵሉ፡ ሕያው፡
verses.text_aramaic: וקדמיתא קרין לה מדנחא דהיא קדמיתא ותניתא קרין לה ימינא דבה כפיף ידא דכל חי
verses.translit: u-qadmaytāʾ qārēn lāh madnāḥāʾ dī-hīʾ qadmaytāʾ u-tinyāytāʾ qārēn lāh yāminā dī-bāh kāpēp yědāʾ dī-kol ḥay
verses.text_geez: ወቀዳማይተ፡ ይሰምይዋ፡ ምሥራቅ፡ እስመ፡ ቀዳማይት፡ ይእቲ፡ ወካልዕተ፡ ይሰምይዋ፡ ጾታ፡ እስመ፡ ህየ፡ ይትዐመጽ፡ እጅገ፡ ኵሉ፡ ሕያው፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q210 frag 1 col. iii lines 1-5 preserves Aramaic of the four-quarter naming + south-as-yamin (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 pp. 167-170; Drawnel 2011 pp. 296-300)
verses.notes: **THE FOUR QUARTERS NAMED.** First = MIZRAḤ (east) 'because it is first.' Second = SOUTH (Aramaic: yamin, right-hand; Ge'ez: ṣota) 'because there [southward] the hand of every living being is humbled' — possibly: 'where the Most High bows down,' i.e. south where the sun reaches its meridian-zenith. Etymological-mythic frame. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Ezek 47-48 (the four-quarter division of the eschatological land); cf. Rev 21:13 (12 gates by direction).

verses.text_geez: ወሣልስተ፡ ይሰምይዋ፡ ምዕራብ፡ እስመ፡ ህየ፡ ይትዓፀዉ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ ብርሃናተ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወይትገብኡ፡ ህየ፡ ለዐሪብ፡ ወአርባዕተ፡ ይሰምይዋ፡ ሰሜን፡ እስመ፡ በውስቴታ፡ ይትኀብኡ፡ ኵሉ፡ ግብረ፡ ኪሩቤል፡ ወሰረፊኤል፡ ወዐራፉ፡ ለልዑል፡
verses.translit: wa-śāləsta yəsamməyəwwā məʿrāb ʾəsma həya yətʿaḍḍawu kwəlomu bərhānāta samāy wa-yətgabbəʾu həya la-ʿarīb wa-ʾarbāʿta yəsamməyəwwā samēn ʾəsma ba-wəstētā yətḫabəʾu kwəlu gəbra Kirubēl wa-Saraffʾēl wa-ʿarāfu la-Ləʿul
verses.witness_primary: Aramaic 4Q210 frag 1 col. iii lines 4-7 (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 pp. 168-170)
verses.text_aramaic: ותליתיתא קרין לה מערבא די תמן עזלין כל נהורי שמיא ותתבון תמן למערב ורביעיתא קרין לה צפונא די בה מסתתרין כל עבדי כרובים ושרפים ובה משכנא דעליא
verses.notes: **Third = MA'ARAV (west) 'because there all the lights of heaven are gathered in and set.'** Fourth = SAFON (north) 'in which all the works of the Cherubim and Seraphim are hidden, and [there is] the dwelling of the Most High.' **CROSS-CORPUS**: the NORTH as divine abode is a major Second Temple cosmographic claim, drawn from Isa 14:13 ('I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far north [yarkəteē ṣapōn]'); cf. Ps 48:2 (Mt. Zion 'in the far north'); cf. Ezek 1:4 (the theophany comes from the north). The Cherubim-Seraphim-throne placement in the north is foundational to the throne-vision tradition of 1 En 14, Ezek 1, Isa 6, Rev 4.

verses.text_geez: ወአፍላገ፡ ምድር፡ ሠለስቱ፡ እማንቱ፡ ቀዳማይት፡ መንገለ፡ ምሥራቅ፡ ወካዕብት፡ መንገለ፡ ጾታ፡ ወሣልስት፡ መንገለ፡ ምዕራብ፡
verses.translit: wa-ʾaflāga mədr śallastu ʾəmāntu qadāmāyət mangala məśrāq wa-kāʿbət mangala ṣotā wa-śāləst mangala məʿrāb
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic 4Q210 frag 1 col. iii lines 7-9 partial (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 p. 170)
verses.notes: **Three sections of earth: east, south, west.** Note: only 3 — the north is the divine-quarter, distinct from the human-habitation regions. This 3+1 geography is distinctive.

verses.text_geez: ወርእኩ፡ ሰብዐ፡ አድባረ፡ ዐበይተ፡ እምነ፡ ኵሉ፡ አድባር፡ ዘውስተ፡ ምድር፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይወፅእ፡ አስሐትዮ፡ ወመዋዕል፡ ወጊዜያት፡ ወዓመታት፡ ይነግሁ፡
verses.text_aramaic: וחזית שבעה טורין רברבין מן כל טוריא די בארעא מנהון נפק תליגא ויומיא ועדניא ושניא יחלפון
verses.translit: u-ḥăzēt šibʿāh ṭūrīn rabrěbīn min kol ṭūrayyāʾ dī bě-ʾarʿāʾ minhōn nāpēq taligāʾ wě-yōmayyāʾ wě-ʿiddānayyāʾ wě-šinnayyāʾ yāḥalpōn
verses.text_geez: ወርእኩ፡ ሰብዐ፡ አድባረ፡ ዐበይተ፡ እምነ፡ ኵሉ፡ አድባር፡ ዘውስተ፡ ምድር፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ይወፅእ፡ አስሐትዮ፡ ወመዋዕል፡ ወጊዜያት፡ ወዓመታት፡ ይነግሁ፡
verses.witness_primary: 4Q210 frag 1 col. iii lines 10-13 preserves 'seven great mountains' (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 pp. 167-170; Drawnel 2011 pp. 300-305)
verses.notes: **SEVEN GREAT MOUNTAINS** — Aramaic ṭūrīn rabrěbīn — from which snow + ages + times + years roll forth. **CROSS-CORPUS**: the seven-mountains cosmography of the apocalyptic tradition: cf. 1 En 24-25 (the seven mountains of the cosmic throne-mountain complex with the tree-of-life at the seventh); cf. Rev 17:9 ('the seven mountains'). Mesopotamian background: the cosmic-mountain idea (Mt. Hashur, Mt. Mashu in Gilgamesh).

verses.text_geez: ወሰብዐ፡ አፍላግ፡ ዐበይተ፡ ርእኩ፡ እምነ፡ ኵሉ፡ አፍላግ፡ ቀዳማይ፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ዘይትበሀል፡ ቤረሳ፡ ወካዕብ፡ ጤግሮስ፡ ወሣልስ፡ ኤፍራጢስ፡
verses.translit: wa-sabʿa ʾaflāg ʿabayta rəʾku ʾəmənna kwəlu ʾaflāg qadāmāyə ʾəmənnehomu ʿabəy zayətbahal Bērasā wa-kāʿb Ṭēgros wa-śāləs ʾĒfraṭīs
verses.witness_primary: Aramaic 4Q210 frag 1 col. iii lines 13-15 partial — preserves names of rivers (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000)
verses.text_aramaic: ושבעה נהרין רברבין חזית מן כל נהריא קדמיא מנהון רבא דאקרי גיחון ותנינא דקלת ותליתיא פרת
verses.notes: **SEVEN GREAT RIVERS.** The first three: Bērasā (Ge'ez corruption; likely Gihon ←→ Aramaic Geon/Gihon), Tigris (Aramaic dqlt/Ḥiddeqel), Euphrates (Pěrāt). **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Gen 2:10-14 (the four Eden rivers: Pishon, Gihon, Hiddekel/Tigris, Euphrates). The Astronomical Book lists SEVEN rivers, extending the Edenic four. cf. Mesopotamian sacred-rivers tradition.

verses.text_geez: ወካልዓኖሙ፡ ምዕራብ፡ ሐራሞን፡ ወካልዕ፡ ኖሉ፡ ወዘ፡ ይትበሀል፡ ጊሐን፡ ወውስተ፡ ምድረ፡ ግብጽ፡ ይነግሥ፡ ወይነግሥ፡ እምነ፡ መንግሥት፡ ለመንግሥት፡
verses.translit: wa-kāləʿānomu məʿrāb ḥarāmon wa-kāləʿ Nolu wa-zə yətbahal Gīḥan wa-wəsta mədra Gəbṣ yənaggəś wa-yənaggəś ʾəmənna mangəśt la-mangəśt
verses.witness_secondary: Aramaic 4Q210 frag 1 col. iii fragmentary (Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000)
verses.notes: **Continuation of the seven rivers — likely including the NILE (Ge'ez 'Nolu' = Nile)** flowing through Egypt. The Ge'ez here is textually corrupt; Charles 1912 attempts reconstruction. The 'Gihan' likely corresponds to the Eden-river GIHON.

verses.text_geez: ወሰብዐ፡ አዕያት፡ ዐበይተ፡ ርእኩ፡ ዐበይተ፡ እምነ፡ ኵሉ፡ ዘውስተ፡ ምድር፡ ቀዳማይ፡ በባሕር፡ ዘሰሜን፡ ወካልዕ፡ በባሕር፡ ዘምዕራብ፡ ወሣልስ፡ በባሕር፡ ዘይትበሀል፡ ኤሪትራ፡
verses.translit: wa-sabʿa ʾaʿyāt ʿabayta rəʾku ʿabayta ʾəmənna kwəlu zawəsta mədr qadāmāyə ba-bāḥr zasamēn wa-kāləʿ ba-bāḥr zaməʿrāb wa-śāləs ba-bāḥr zayətbahal ʾĒritrā
verses.notes: **SEVEN GREAT ISLANDS** in the great sea. First two seas, then the Erythraean Sea (Red Sea). The Erythraean naming is Hellenistic Greek for the Red Sea + Persian Gulf area — a HELLENISTIC-PERIOD GEOGRAPHIC NAME indicating the Aramaic Astronomical Book's circulation in the Greek-influenced Eastern Mediterranean.

verses.text_geez: ወዘስብእ፡ ኆለቆሙ፡ ለሐይኮት፡ ስብእ፡ መንበራቶሙ፡ ለዕለታት፡ ወአሐደ፡ መንበር፡ ዐባዪ፡ ላዕሌሁ፡ ይሰምይ፡ መንበሮሙ፡ ለኪሩቤል፡ ኅዱረ፡ ዘይነብር፡ ዐርእስት፡ ዘይኬልሉ፡ ለመንበራቲሁ፡
verses.translit: wa-zasəbʾ ḫolaqomu la-ḥaykot səbʾ manbarātomu la-ʿəlatāt wa-ʾaḥada manbar ʿabāyə lāʿlēhu yəsammə manbaromu la-Kirubēl ḫədura zayənabbər ʿarʾəst zayəkēlalu la-manbarātihu
verses.notes: **Cherubim throne reference** — at the center of the seven-mountains cosmography. Charles 1912 notes this verse may be partially out of sequence (textual disturbance). Cross-corpus: cf. 1 En 14:18-20 (the throne-vision); cf. Ezek 10.

verses.text_geez: ወሰብዐ፡ አዕያት፡ ዐበይተ፡ ርእኩ፡ ዘመሐልዮ፡ ኮኑ፡ ሠለስቱ፡ መንገለ፡ ምሥራቅ፡ ወክልኤቱ፡ መንገለ፡ ጾታ፡ ወክልኤቱ፡ መንገለ፡ ምዕራብ፡
verses.translit: wa-sabʿa ʾaʿyāt ʿabayta rəʾku zamaḥalyo konu śallastu mangala məśrāq wa-kəlʾētu mangala ṣotā wa-kəlʾētu mangala məʿrāb
verses.notes: **3 + 2 + 2 = 7 islands distributed across the cardinal directions.** Closing distribution-summary for the seven-island enumeration.
